stem.text: The temperature T of a metal rod, in degrees Celsius, placed in a chamber held at 75 degrees Celsius moves toward the chamber temperature at a rate proportional to the difference between the chamber temperature and T. At time \( t = 0 \) minutes, \( T = 55 \). Using k for the positive constant of proportionality, write a differential equation for T as a function of t and state the initial condition.

worked_solution.text: The dependent variable is T and the independent variable is t in minutes, so the rate is \( \frac{dT}{dt} \).

Proportional to the difference means a constant multiple of it. With k positive, \( k(75 - T) \) is positive when T is below 75 and negative when it is above, so T moves up toward 75 from its starting value.
The equation is \( \frac{dT}{dt} = k\left(75 - T\right) \), and the initial condition, stated separately, is \( T(0) = 55 \).

options.label: \( \frac{dT}{dt} = k\left(T - 75\right) \), with \( T(0) = 55 \)
options.derivation: the difference written as T minus the level, which with k positive drives T away from 75

options.label: \( \frac{dT}{dt} = k\left(75 - 55\right) \), with \( T(0) = 55 \)
options.derivation: the initial value 55 substituted for T inside the equation, so the rate becomes a constant

options.label: \( \frac{dT}{dt} = 75 - T \), with \( T(0) = 55 \)
options.derivation: proportional read as equal, so the constant k never appears
